text:
Maya: Heads up — alert from autoscaler in us-west. Request queue spiked and tail latency jumped. GPUs are hot on a few nodes while others are nearly idle. Suspect scheduler head-of-line blocking. Anyone seeing this?

Jon K: Yup, seeing the same. queues_per_pool jumped from 2->18 in ~3m. kube-scheduler logs show repeated placement retries and long lease waits.

Rafael: This might be related to the placement policy flip we rolled last week (binpack -> balanced). Not sure it's respecting pod priorities for batch jobs.

Anya: We saw a similar pattern on dedicated pools yesterday — large batch jobs get to the front and then hog entire GPU pods, starving smaller interactive requests.

Chris: I'm going to restart the scheduler on the canary control plane in us-west to see if it unsticks. Doing now.

deploy-bot: restart: kube-scheduler/us-west control-plane restarted by Chris at 2026-03-10T14:15:30Z :white_check_mark:

Chris: Restarted scheduler. Queues are draining, utilization across nodes is evening out. Looks like a scheduling loop or a cache inconsistency that the restart cleared.

Maya: Good quick fix — but we need a proper root cause. Rafael can you capture the config diff from last week and any scheduler metrics that indicate head-of-line blocking vs miscomputed admission control? Add a repro if possible.

Rafael: Created issue #3421 in eng-runtime: "scheduler: head-of-line blocking with balanced-placement causing uneven GPU utilization". Steps to reproduce, logs, and a small repro job are attached. Assigning to eng-runtime. ETA: 48h for a diagnostic patch + tests.

Leo: For short-term mitigation I recommend enabling per-customer admission caps and a fairness window so a single long job can't starve the queue. We can also set a queue timeout that preempts oversized jobs after N seconds.

Anya: We already have a feature flag `fair_admission` in cluster-config. Can flip it for dedicated pools in us-west only. That should throttle large batches immediately.

Maya: Ok Anya, flip `fair_admission` in us-west dedicated and run a smoke test. Jon K, can you add a derived dashboard metric for per-node active_jobs_variance and an alert if variance > 0.6? Rafael, add unit/integration tests for the balanced placement code path.

Jon K: Will add the chart and alert (dashboard id will be linked in the issue).

Rafael: Adding tests and a canary rollout plan to the issue. Also adding a trace of lease/grant delays to help confirm root cause.

Chris: We should also capture core dumps and keep the restarted scheduler logs for postmortem. I've archived logs to s3://redwood-ops/scheduler-restarts/1760841234.tar.gz.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Short checklist: (1) Anya flips flag + smoke test, (2) Jon adds alert, (3) Rafael posts PR for fix, (4) keep restart logs. We'll follow up in the issue and circle back in the next infra sync. :thumbsup:
